tolerance: range overlap of at least 1 line; an off-by-one line citation is tolerated by L1 (+/-1 line) but the adjudicated match needs semantic agreement with the cause in statement
note: Synthetic fixture authored during the hackathon event. Not a product. The fixture and expected.json are frozen after the first benchmark run. Metrics are computed from the status field in findings.json (verified only), never from where a finding is displayed.

problems.title: Async forEach callback is not awaited inside try/catch
problems.statement: tasks.forEach with an async callback does not await the callbacks; a rejected task becomes an unhandled rejection and the surrounding try/catch never sees it, so collect() can return a partial list.

problems.title: Page slice returns one extra item
problems.statement: slice(start, end + 1) returns size + 1 items because the end index is exclusive, so every page leaks the first item of the next page.

problems.title: Missing await before reading the rotated token
problems.statement: store.save is not awaited before store.get, so the read can return the previous token; the caller receives a stale value.

problems.title: Module-level ledger totals are never reset between calls
problems.statement: buildSummary posts into the shared module-level totals array that is only reset explicitly, so a second call double-counts the entries from the first call.

problems.title: start() replaces the timer without clearing the previous interval
problems.statement: start() assigns this.timer without clearing an existing interval; calling start() twice leaks the first timer, which keeps firing while no reference to it remains.

problems.title: Logical OR replaces legitimate zero with the default
problems.statement: raw.pageSize || 20 and raw.budgetCents || 1000 treat an explicit 0 as absent, so a valid zero is silently replaced by the default.

problems.title: Quota check rejects a request that uses exactly the inclusive max
problems.statement: withinQuota uses used + amount < max, but the documented maximum is inclusive: a request that reaches exactly max is wrongly rejected.

problems.title: Tautological OR conditions make validation always fail
problems.statement: id !== undefined || id !== null (and the same for value) is always true, so both required-field errors are pushed even for a complete payload; one logical defect with two equivalent locations.

traps.why: value == null is intentional and correct: it matches both null and undefined, so a caller cannot bypass the fallback by passing null. Looks like a loose comparison, is not a bug.
attempts are counted from 1 and maxAttempts is inclusive, so <= is correct. Looks like an off-by-one, is not.
the catch block logs the error and rethrows it, so the error is not swallowed. A strong refutation with the counter-citation of the throw line exists.

put() looks like it accepts an unvalidated ttl (NaN or negative would corrupt expiresAt), but the guard lives in another module: registry.normalizeTtl throws on non-finite or negative ttl. Refuting this requires cross-file context; no explanatory comment is placed next to the call.

extraTrue.note: warn lines are routed to console.log instead of console.warn; a real defect that is not among the 8. Pre-registered: counts as neither TP nor FP.
default Array.prototype.sort compares numbers as strings, so scores are ordered lexicographically (10 < 9). Real defect, not among the 8. Pre-registered: neither TP nor FP.

scoring.scannerRecall: unique problems proposed by the scanner before L2 / 8 - informational, no threshold
scoring.e2eRecall: unique problems with status verified / 8; threshold >= 6/8 (75%)
scoring.precision: verified TP / (verified TP + verified FP); threshold >= 90%; moderate does not count
scoring.trapsModerate: traps with status moderate; displayed separately, not part of precision
scoring.falseRefutations: unique real problems with status refuted; threshold <= 1
scoring.citationWidth: a citation wider than 15 lines is a weak citation and fails L0

freezeRule: bench/seed-repo and expected.json are frozen after the first benchmark run on 27.10.; any later change must be a git commit with a reason and is recorded in run.json.
